text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to $131.83, continuing a sharp downward swing from last Tuesday's high of $141.22. The immediate pressure came from oil prices dropping as traders reassessed Middle East supply disruptions—crude fell Monday despite ongoing geopolitical tensions because actual oil flows from Saudi Arabia remained stronger than feared, suggesting the conflict may not crimp global supplies as severely as initially worried. The stock has now given back most of a week's gains in just three trading days.

The broader backdrop is that oil investors are caught between two opposing forces: geopolitical risk (Iran keeping the Strait of Hormuz closed, Houthi attacks, rising U.S.-Iran tensions) and the reality that supply disruptions so far have proven less severe than the headlines implied. As long as crude can flow and traders see the worst-case scenario as less likely, energy stocks like COP face downward pressure even amid Middle East instability.
